summary.en: Bandits attacked a mining site in Plateau, killing three people, and carried out fresh killings that left nine dead in another Plateau attack. The Nigerian army met with bandits in Kwara, recording a video that was later clarified as surrender talks rather than fraternisation, while a separate viral video showed soldiers interacting with armed bandits. U.S. officials praised Nigeria for rescuing 125 victims and dismantling terrorist camps, and Nigerian forces killed 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno. Police are searching for the family of a Canadian-Nigerian man killed in a road crash in Lagos. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter angrep en gruveplass i Plateau, drepte tre personer, og gjennomførte nye drap som førte til ni døde i et annet angrep i Plateau. Den nigerianske hæren møtte banditter i Kwara, og en video som ble spredt ble senere klargjort som forhandlinger om overgivelse snarere enn fraternisering, mens en separat viral video viste soldater som interagerte med bevæpnede banditter. Amerikanske tjenestemenn roste Nigeria for å ha reddet 125 ofre og demontert terrorleirer, og nigerianske styrker drepte 21 ISWAP-krigere i Borno. Politiet leter etter familien til en kanadisk-nigerisk mann som ble drept i en veitrafikkulykke i Lagos. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
